body: Several of us in Finance take undergrad RAs each semester. Send a short note with your coursework and one question you find interesting, and attach a résumé.
Our lab is looking for someone comfortable with Python and basic statistics. Learning pandas before you reach out is a big plus!
I got my start as an RA pulling CRSP data for a Finance professor sophomore year. It's the single best line on my résumé for quant interviews, so go for it.
Try the third floor of WALC after 9pm, or the Hicks basement. Both are much quieter.
The reading room in the Ag Library in Lilly Hall is almost empty at night. Bring a jacket though, it's always cold.
You don't need CS 373 first; a finished PyTorch project matters more to me. Email me a link to your code and which of our recent papers interested you.
Most of our undergrads start by reproducing one result from a paper over a few weeks. Also check the CS undergraduate research page and the Purdue OUR listings.
We take students with zero bench experience every semester since we train everyone on sterile technique ourselves. Reliability and a consistent weekly schedule matter far more than prior skills.
Read two or three recent papers from the lab and show up curious. Taking BIOL 23100 or a lab-based course alongside helps you follow lab meetings.
Do two LeetCode mediums a day and practice talking out loud while you code. We care about how you communicate trade-offs as much as the final answer.
Purdue Hackers runs mock interviews on Thursdays in LWSN, they helped me a lot last year.
Totally worth it for me. Almost every co-op who performs well gets a full-time offer, and you start with real seniority on engine programs.
The extra semester usually pays for itself in salary and experience. Talk to the Purdue co-op office about keeping your ME course sequence on track between rotations.
One year is a good start, but most admitted clinical applicants have two or more years plus an honors thesis or poster. A post-bacc research job is common and is viewed positively.
I did a two-year research coordinator job before getting in and it made my statement much stronger. Present at the Purdue Undergraduate Research Conference if you can.
I did the combined BS/MS and finished a year faster than friends who left and came back. If you already know your specialty, staying is efficient.
Work experience helps you choose a focus but rarely changes funding for MS students. If you want a research MS, start talking to potential advisors this semester.
Ask anyway, and acknowledge the grade directly when you do. A strong lab performance and evidence of growth often make a more convincing letter than an easy A.
At a startup you'll own entire projects in your first month, but negotiate equity terms clearly and keep some savings. If the founders have farm customers already, that's a good sign.
The daily market notebook idea is great, starting one this week for my paper portfolio.
This is really helpful. I'll rewrite my email to name a specific paper before sending it.
